entries.title: Smooth deterministic reflected-Brownian maps are Euclidean isometries [draft; pending w347]
entries.statement: Let D be a bounded connected C^2 domain in R^d and F:D->D a C^2 diffeomorphism. If, for every initial x in D, normal reflected Brownian motion X started at x has F(X_t) with the normal reflected-Brownian law started at F(x), then F(x)=Qx+b for a fixed orthogonal Q and b. The conclusion uses smoothness, an onto map, and all starting points; it does not classify arbitrary measurable deterministic maps or convert every shy coupling to a deterministic one.
entries.proof_text:
At an interior starting point the small-time covariance of F(X_t)-F(x), divided by t, tends to DF(x)*DF(x)^T by Ito's formula (reflection has no first-order effect before the boundary is hit). The corresponding limit for a reflected Brownian motion started at the interior point F(x) is the identity. Thus DF*DF^T=I at every x. Since DF is square, it is orthogonal, so its columns e_i=partial_i F form an orthonormal basis.

Set A_ijk=<partial_i partial_j F,e_k>. Equality of mixed partials gives A_ijk=A_jik. Differentiating <e_j,e_k>=delta_jk gives A_ijk=-A_ikj. Combining the two symmetries,

    A_ijk = A_jik = -A_jki = -A_kji
           = A_kij = A_ikj = -A_ijk,

so every A_ijk is zero. The e_k span R^d, hence every second derivative of F is zero. On a connected open domain this makes DF a fixed orthogonal matrix Q and F-Qx a constant b. This establishes rigidity under the stated regularity and all-starting-points assumptions.
assumptions: C^2 diffeomorphism from D onto D
Normal Brownian covariance in the interior
Reflected law preserved for every initial point

entries.title: Positive displacement characterizes shy isometry couplings [draft; pending w347]
entries.statement: Let F(x)=Qx+b be a Euclidean isometry preserving a bounded connected smooth domain D. Suppose normal reflected Brownian motion X in D almost surely visits every nonempty interior open set infinitely often. Then Y=F(X) is a reflected-Brownian coupling, and it is shy if and only if min_{closure D}|x-F(x)|>0. A bounded convex preserving domain has a fixed centroid and therefore no shy isometry coupling. A planar annulus with inner radius R>0 and nontrivial rotation theta has separation at least 2R*|sin(theta/2)|. No claim about arbitrary nondeterministic shy couplings is made.
entries.proof_text:
For an isometry F preserving D, normal reflection is equivariant: Q sends Brownian noise to Brownian noise and the inward normal at x to the inward normal at F(x). Thus F(X) has the reflected law. Suppose also that X visits every nonempty interior open set infinitely often almost surely, as normal reflected Brownian motion does in a bounded smooth connected domain. Then the deterministic isometry coupling is shy exactly when

    min_{x in closure D} |x-F(x)| > 0.

If the minimum is positive the distance stays uniformly positive. If it is zero, for every epsilon>0 the set {x in D: |x-F(x)|<epsilon} is nonempty and open by continuity and density of D in its closure. Recurrence forces visits to it. Applying this to epsilon=1/k shows inf_t |X_t-F(X_t)|=0 almost surely, ruling out shyness.

If D is convex, its volume centroid c lies in D. Any preserving Euclidean isometry fixes c: change variables in its centroid integral to obtain Qc+b=c. Therefore this regular deterministic class has no shy coupling on a bounded convex smooth domain. This is not a claim about all nondeterministic couplings on such a domain.

On the annulus R<|x|<R_out in R^2, 0<R<R_out, rotation by theta has minimum displacement 2R*|sin(theta/2)|. Every nontrivial rotation modulo 2*pi is therefore a deterministic shy coupling. The prior antipodal example is theta=pi. Letting R=0 or theta=0 removes the positive-gap check.
assumptions: Recurrence to every nonempty interior open set
